title: Sections over a weakly contractible affine preserve colimits
statement:
Let $W$ be an affine weakly contractible object of a pro-étale site and $A$ a sheaf of rings. The functor
$M\mapsto\Gamma(W,M)$ from sheaves of $A$-modules to abelian groups is exact and preserves all colimits; in
particular filtered colimits and direct sums.

proof.text: Put $R=A(W)$. Apply [det-pe-sections-limits-colimits] with the given ring sheaf $A$ and affine weakly contractible $W$. It gives preservation of all limits and all colimits for the module-valued evaluation $E:M\mapsto M(W)$. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], morphisms evaluate to $R$-linear maps and evaluation is additive: $(f+g)_W=f_W+g_W$. The hypotheses use weak contractibility of the site object, without assuming that its coordinate ring is w-contractible, and impose no commutativity on $A$.

source.place: First paragraph, exact sections; the existing stronger sections theorem also supplies the direct-sum and colimit conclusions.

proof.text: Let $0\to M\xrightarrow{f}N\xrightarrow{g}P\to0$ be short exact in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its first map is a kernel of $g$ and its second is a cokernel of $f$. The limit and colimit preservation of Step 1 give the same kernel and cokernel diagrams in $R$-modules. A kernel of an $R$-linear map is its subgroup of elements sent to zero, with the restricted action; a cokernel is the quotient by its image, with the quotient action. Their underlying additive groups are therefore the abelian-group kernel and cokernel as well. Hence $0\to M(W)\to N(W)\to P(W)\to0$ is short exact in abelian groups. This proves the stated exactness.

source.place: First paragraph, exactness, with the passage from module values to underlying abelian groups written explicitly.

proof.text: For any small diagram $D:I\to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$, form $B=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathrm{Ob}I}D(i)$ and $C=\bigoplus_{u:i\to j}D(i)$ on underlying additive groups, and define $d:C\to B$ on the $u$-summand by $x\mapsto\iota_jD(u)(x)-\iota_i(x)$. Direct sums carry coordinatewise $R$-action; $d$ is linear, so $L=B/\operatorname{im}d$ carries the quotient action. By [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], $L$ is the colimit both in modules and in abelian groups: a homomorphism $B\to H$ is a family $h_i$, and it kills $d$ exactly when $h_jD(u)=h_i$ for each arrow; if $H$ is a module and the $h_i$ are linear, the induced quotient map is linear. Thus the forgetful functor to abelian groups preserves these colimit cocones. Apply this to $D=E\circ F$ for any small diagram $F$ of $A$-module sheaves: Step 1 identifies $E(\operatorname{colim}F)$ with this module colimit, with the evaluated cocone maps. After forgetting, it is still the colimit cocone, so its comparison into abelian groups is exactly the canonical isomorphism. This includes the empty diagram, for which $B=C=L=0$, every discrete diagram (direct sums), and every filtered diagram.

source.place: Second paragraph, explicit cokernel presentation; same presentation proves preservation when forgetting the section-ring action.

proof_origin.place: The two blueprint proof paragraphs, reusing the stronger result det-pe-sections-limits-colimits of the explicitly cited sk-cor-pe-sections unit, and writing out the underlying additive-group passage.
